paragraphs: In the preprint Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation, submitted to arXiv on November 4, an Apple research team introduced HALO. The system lets a humanoid robot use its own cameras and natural-language instructions to find targets, sit, open doors, crouch, crawl and push boxes in indoor spaces that have not been scanned in advance. The project page and code repository are public.

The system divides work into three layers: a vision-language model decomposes instructions roughly every two seconds; a motion generator replans five seconds of whole-body motion at about 3 Hz; and a low-level tracker executes the plan at 50 Hz using depth images and proprioception. Training primarily uses **300 hours of simulated task data from 1,000 procedurally generated homes**, linking language, first-person images and human motion.

paragraphs: 【2020 Representative Works Review | Public Abstract and Author Selection Excerpts】Pedersen, Chen, and Zhu proposed a design process for preventing ship collisions with bridge piers and bridge towers: first, clarify the risk acceptance criteria, then calculate the hazardous encounters in the bridge area and the probability of collisions caused by human and technical errors, thereby determining the design ship that each bridge pier must be able to withstand.

The structural analysis section calculates the force-displacement relationship of the bow impact rigid wall for different ship types and tonnages, and establishes an empirical relationship for the maximum bow impact force based on this. The authors compare the new relationship with existing expressions for ice zone strengthened ships and design standards, while also providing a local pressure-area relationship for the bulbous bow impact, which is used to distinguish overall load requirements from local contact pressure.

The key feature of this work is to connect traffic risks with structural resistance, rather than first selecting the largest ship and then only calculating a peak force. The author's draft also emphasizes that bridge construction will alter navigation organization, and impact assessments must take this change into account. The bow resistance here originates from the scenario of rigid wall collapse and cannot be directly used as a complete response for flexible bridge piers, oblique collisions, or floating bridges; the deformation of the impacted structure and the hydrodynamic forces still require corresponding models. This work did not include the author's comparison with the old standards, and it was not stated that all current standards have become obsolete.

paragraphs: [Zhang et al. 2020, 2021 representative works review | public abstract reading] Zhang et al. combined the external dynamic model of ship–semi-submersible wind turbine collision with their self-developed DARwind time-domain program to study the system response of a 5 MW Spar wind turbine. The cases were respectively conducted under calm water, only wave, and combined wave and wind conditions, focusing on the response changes of the platform, mooring, tower, blades, and nacelle.

In calm water, ship collision significantly affects the motion of the platform and the mooring response; under only wave conditions, waves have a dampening effect on some parts of the platform motion, but the tower vibration and tower top deformation are still sensitive to collision. After adding wind, the increments of heave and pitch caused by collision are relatively small, but there is a significant change in the initial yaw. The increments in tip vortex motion in the direction of flap and pitch are also different.

The cabin acceleration analysis shows that even when the structure is not severely damaged, internal equipment may still be unable to function normally due to the acceleration induced by impact. The value of this paper lies in incorporating the continuous dynamic response after a short contact into the safety evaluation, rather than using the local damage at the moment of impact to judge the operational status. Based on the institutional summary, it is not considered that the external dynamic method adopted is fully reconstructed to represent the local shell fracture, and it is also not considered that the inhibitory effect in individual environmental conditions can be generalized to reduce the collision risk overall.
